description: DEBUGHUSTLERZ is a team of passionate students interested in technology, space science, AI, robotics, and innovation. We bring skills in C++, Python, electronics, Arduino, ESP32, and problem-solving. We believe in teamwork, creativity, and turning ideas into practical solutions. We are looking for enthusiastic teammates skilled in AI/ML, data science, web development, UI/UX, GIS, astronomy, and research. Above all, we value curiosity, dedication, and a willingness to learn.
summary: Mars Outpost: Astro-Engineer is a 3D browser-based survival game designed to teach young learners about the harsh engineering trade-offs of space exploration. Players take on the role of a Junior Commander managing a Martian outpost. They must navigate a fully realized 3D environment, switching between three distinct roles (Engineer, Explorer, Medic) to complete 50 critical repair tasks across massive futuristic facilities. Players are forced to balance Oxygen and Base Power while surviving random catastrophic events like Martian dust storms and solar flares. Built entirely with Three.js and procedural generation, the game provides immediate, accessible fun while subtly teaching core STEM principles about life support, resource management, and the unforgiving nature of the Red Planet.
details: The game addresses the challenge by making the complex, invisible trade-offs of space survival tangible in a 3D space. Kids don't just read about life support; they have to physically run across a Martian landscape to choose whether to fix the oxygen scrubbers or repair the solar array while a dust storm rages outside. We used Three.js (WebGL), HTML5, and CSS3 for the game engine, UI, and state management. The logic dictates a base degradation rate, forcing the player to prioritize tasks and switch roles dynamically (1: Engineer, 2: Explorer, 3: Medic). The game features a dynamic third-person camera, custom Martian sky shaders, particle-based weather systems, and massive interactive structures with animated sliding doors. It is creative because it wraps hard science in a fast, replayable, and visually stunning arcade-style loop.
